answer: Single-use challenge provenance. Each task a new agent performs includes a violet nonce derived from the prior task's output, which the agent must extend through a crystal hash chain stored only in its working memory. To reach the reputation zenith that unlocks paid work, it must complete a fresh randomized chain for every transaction, and each chain demands unique computation whose result is discarded after one use. An attacker replaying captured responses triggers nonce mismatch; cloning identities means recomputing every chain from scratch, so cost scales linearly with identity count.
